findings.claim: detectProvider drops the fail-fast 'Multiple crypto providers loaded' IllegalStateException and picks the highest order(); Default, Elytron and FIPS1402 providers all return 200, so a tie between real providers is silently resolved by ServiceLoader/classpath order (losers logged only at DEBUG). A FIPS deployment with a stray crypto-default jar can now silently run on non-FIPS BC instead of failing at startup. No test covers the new selection logic.
findings.evidence: DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83, WildFlyElytronProvider.java:76, FIPS1402Provider.java:114 all return 200; Stream.sorted is stable. Affected callers of CryptoIntegration.init: services KeycloakApplication.java:89, admin-cli Globals.java:44 (dist ships default+fips1402 jars), testsuite CryptoInitRule, AuthzClient.create. Quarkus unaffected (KeycloakRecorder.java:214 uses setProvider). Proposed red test: two order-200 providers on ServiceLoader path, assert init throws (throws on base, returns provider on HEAD). Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Raised independently by both correctness seats and the standards seat with source citations; the authz stub only needs to lose to real providers (100 vs 200), so keep throwing when the top two orders are equal.

findings.claim: int order() is added as an abstract method on the public keycloak-common CryptoProvider SPI, breaking source compatibility and causing AbstractMethodError in detectProvider's comparator for any externally compiled implementation (e.g. the keycloak-client authz-client copy); no upgrade/migration note.
findings.evidence: CryptoProvider.java:44 'int order();' with no default; CryptoIntegration.java:57 calls CryptoProvider::order on every discovered provider. All in-repo implementations updated. PR-CHECKLIST.md requires upgrade-guide notes where applicable; no docs changes in patch. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Raised Important by a correctness seat (Minor by the others); a default method removes the break at near-zero cost and also removes the three duplicated overrides.

findings.claim: ES256/ES384/ES512 tests all use one default-curve KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key and only assert a self round-trip, so P-384/P-521 widths and the DER long-form length paths (ASN1Encoder.writeLength / ASN1Decoder.readLength > 127) are never exercised, and a symmetric encoder/decoder bug would pass.
findings.evidence: ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 single default key reused; assertion compares rsConcat to rsConcat2 only. SP seat's out-of-repo harness (500 sigs each on P-256/384/521 vs SHAxxxwithECDSAinP1363Format) found 0 failures, so this is a coverage gap, not a codec bug.
findings.reason: Cheap to generate a key per curve and verify against JCA P1363 output; turns a reasoned-correct codec into a guarded one.

findings.claim: Dead code: ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) and ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger) build encoders and discard them; lines 117-121 redo the encoding.
New org.hamcrest:hamcrest test dependency is unused.
findings.evidence: grep -rn hamcrest authz/client/src/test returns nothing; ECDSAAlgorithmTest imports only org.junit.Assert/Test.

findings.claim: Ignored-providers debug line passes a runtime-built string as the debugf format string (a '%' would be misinterpreted) and leaves a trailing ', '.
Identical 'return 200' order() override pasted into DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider because order() has no default.
findings.reason: Resolved by the same default-method fix as the CryptoProvider.java:44 finding.

findings.claim: AuthzClient.create now calls CryptoIntegration.init, setting JVM-global first-caller-wins crypto state; if only the stub provider is visible it is pinned for the JVM (most methods throw UnsupportedOperationException) and getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK keystore provider (e.g. SUN), freezing BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER.
findings.evidence: AuthzClient.java:95; AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61-63 returns KeyStore.getInstance(getDefaultType()).getProvider(); CryptoIntegration.init no-ops once set. On the normal testsuite classpath crypto-default (200) beats the stub (100); module artifact is keycloak-authz-client-tests. No concrete failure found. Reasoned.
findings.reason: No concrete failing configuration in this repo; module is testsuite-only. Settle by running the embedded-undertow testsuite with authz-client initialised first.

findings.claim: Lenient/unchecked DER parsing: tag checks mask with 0x1f ignoring class/constructed bits, trailing bytes ignored, zero-length INTEGER throws NumberFormatException, and indefinite-length (0x80) returns -1 leading to NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException.
findings.evidence: ASN1Decoder.java:52,68,73,94,133-134. Only production input is JCA Signature.sign() output via ECDSASignatureSignerContext (trusted); verifier path only encodes and ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.verify catches Exception.
findings.reason: ponytail: input is trusted JCA DER on the signer path only; tighten (or drop the indefinite-length/high-tag branches) if the decoder ever parses untrusted input.

findings.claim: General-purpose high-tag-number and indefinite-length decoding is unneeded for DER ECDSA signatures (always 0x30 with two 0x02 INTEGERs).
findings.evidence: ASN1Decoder.java:93-124, 133-135; sole caller ECDSASignatureSignerContext.java:33 passes JDK DER output.
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory over-engineering, ~25 lines removable; non-blocking and overlaps the leniency finding above.

findings.evidence: Whitespace-only hunks at CryptoProvider.java:94, DefaultCryptoProvider.java:186, FIPS1402Provider.java:203,208,230,234.
findings.reason: ponytail: harmless trailing-whitespace removal; reverting is pure churn. Note for maintainer at squash.
